summary_ja: クレジット・デリバティブの適格条件として、不払・倒産・リストラクチャリングを信用事由とすること、評価手続、原債権譲渡の同意、信用事由判断者の明確化、参照債務の順位・クロス・デフォルト、CDS又はTRSであること等を定める。
summary_en: Credit derivative conditions: credit events covering failure to pay, bankruptcy and restructuring; robust valuation for cash settlement; transferable underlying obligation; clear credit-event determination; reference obligations pari passu or junior with cross-default; CDS or TRS only.

terms.ja: クロス・デフォルト条項等

paragraphs: Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach uses a credit derivative as a credit risk mitigation technique, the credit derivative shall, in addition to what is provided in Article 94, satisfy all of the following conditions. (i) That payment can be received under the credit derivative upon the occurrence of the following events: (a) Failure to meet payment obligations on the underlying claim (this does not preclude setting a materiality threshold). (b) A decision to commence bankruptcy proceedings, rehabilitation proceedings or reorganization proceedings, an order to commence special liquidation or insolvency relating to the obligor of the underlying claim, or the existence of a document certifying that it is extremely likely to default when the underlying claim falls due, or similar events. (c) A reduction of, or a moratorium on, payments of principal, interest or fees of the underlying claim made for the purpose of rehabilitating or supporting the obligor of the underlying claim. (ii) That, where the protection provider can settle by calculating the payment amount upon the occurrence of an event listed in the preceding item based on the valuation of a specific obligation of the obligor of the underlying claim and paying it in cash, procedures for properly carrying out that valuation (including a set period until the valuation is carried out) have been established. (iii) That, where the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach is obliged to transfer the underlying claim to the protection provider for settlement upon the occurrence of an event listed in item (i), and that transfer requires the consent of the obligor of the underlying claim, the documents relating to the underlying claim provide that such consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. (iv) That the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach has the right to notify the protection provider of the occurrence of an event listed in item (i), and that the person who determines whether such an event has occurred is clearly specified; provided, however, that this determination may not be one that only the protection provider can make. (v) That, where the underlying claim is not included in the reference obligations for settlement, the reference obligations for settlement rank equal with or subordinate to the underlying claim in order of payment, the obligor of the underlying claim and of the reference obligations for settlement is the same, and the reference obligations for settlement have legally effective cross-default clauses, etc. (meaning clauses that make it possible to accelerate the reference obligations where an event listed in item (i) occurs on the underlying claim; the same applies in the following item). (vi) That, where the underlying claim is not included in the reference obligations for determining credit events, the reference obligations for determining credit events rank equal with or subordinate to the underlying claim in order of payment, the obligor of the reference obligations for determining credit events and of the underlying claim is the same, and the reference obligations for determining credit events have legally effective cross-default clauses, etc. (vii) That the credit derivative is a credit default swap or total return swap that provides a credit risk mitigation effect equivalent to a guarantee; provided, however, that where the Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach recognizes as income the net receipts received under the total return swap, it is required to recognize the decline in value of the underlying claim through a reduction of the book value or a provision.
